title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Communication with Opposing Party
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal is representing a landlord. The tenant is represented by their own paralegal. The landlord's paralegal is frustrated because the tenant's paralegal is slow to respond to emails. Can the landlord's paralegal contact the tenant directly to speed up settlement negotiations?
options: Yes, as long as they only communicate via written correspondence.
Yes, but only to relay settlement offers without offering legal advice.
No, a paralegal must not communicate directly with a person who is represented by a legal practitioner without that practitioner's consent.
No, unless the landlord's paralegal first notifies the LSO of the opposing representative's delays.
questions.explain: Under Rule 7.02 (Communication with a represented person), a paralegal shall not approach or communicate directly with a person who is represented by a legal practitioner concerning the matter, except with the consent of the legal practitioner.
